title: Process over outcome
subtitle: Judge your decisions, not your P&L

scenes.say: Did you trade well? The answer isn't in your profit and loss. Let's see why the best traders judge the process, not the result.

scenes.title: Four kinds of trades
scenes.say: Every trade falls into one of four boxes. Good process and a win. Good process and a loss, which is still a good trade. Bad process and a win, which is dangerous luck. And bad process with a loss.

scenes.title: Why luck is dangerous
scenes.say: The most dangerous box is the lucky win. It rewards breaking your rules, so you're likely to do it again, until the luck runs out.

els.sub: Rewards teach you to repeat whatever you just did.

scenes.title: Your edge needs a big sample
scenes.say: Any setup can lose several times in a row. Your edge only shows up over many trades. Judge yourself on ten trades and you're judging luck. Judge yourself on a hundred and you'll see your real edge.

scenes.title: Grade the process
scenes.say: So grade the process. Before the trade: did it pass your checklist? During: did you follow the plan and respect the stop? After: give yourself a grade and log your emotions in the journal.

items.label: During
items.sub: Followed the plan and the stop?

scenes.title: Recap
scenes.say: You control the process, not the outcome. Make good decisions again and again, and the results will take care of themselves.

els.sub: Accept the outcome. Good decisions, repeated, produce results.
